headline: Fuel prices surge: All four major petroleum products raised by Tk 20
summary: Diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene prices hit record highs as the government passes on mounting import costs to consumers.
details: The government has increased the prices of all four major petroleum products by Tk 20 per litre, effective from 12:00 am today. This move takes all four fuels to their highest-ever retail prices.
Diesel now costs Tk 135 per litre, octane Tk 165, petrol Tk 160, and kerosene Tk 155. This is the third fuel price hike since the BNP-led government took office in February.

The hike is driven by rising international petroleum prices and freight charges, which have surged since March due to ongoing global conflicts. Brent crude has recently crossed the $100-a-barrel mark.
The Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) reported a loss of Tk 22,875 crore between March and August, losing around Tk 89 on every litre of diesel sold before this adjustment.
Diesel is critical to the economy, accounting for 64% of total petroleum consumption. It is heavily used in transport (60%), agriculture (15%), and power generation (10%).
Experts warn that higher diesel prices will likely lead to a second-round impact on food and other consumer goods prices as transport and distribution costs increase.
Despite the increase, the BPC had proposed a retail diesel price of Tk 187 per litre for September to fully cover import costs, but the government refrained from passing the full cost to consumers.

headline_marked: 7 dead after [[gas cylinder blast in Ashulia]] lorry fire
headline: 7 dead after gas cylinder blast in Ashulia lorry fire
summary: Four Pretty Group factories were shut down following a deadly explosion and fire in a lorry parked in the group's designated parking area.
details: At least seven people were killed after a gas cylinder exploded in a lorry parked in the parking area of Pretty Group factories in Jamgora, Ashulia.
The blast triggered a massive fire that destroyed several vehicles in the open parking area used for transporting goods.
Four factories—Pretty Composite Textile Ltd, Pretty Composite Garments Ltd, Oxford Colours Ltd, and S Suhi Industrial Park Ltd—were shut down for one day following the incident.
Police confirmed that one body is at the Dhaka Medical College morgue, while six others are at the Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College morgue.
Five of the recovered bodies have not yet been identified. Most of the victims are believed to be employees of the factories' transport section.
Factory buildings remained undamaged, and production was expected to resume the following day after the temporary closure.
Savar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Saiful Islam stated that the Fire Service and Civil Defence and the Department of Labour will form probe committees to investigate the blast.
The upazila administration is assessing the damage and arranging pre-compensation for the families of the deceased.
caption:
A gas cylinder blast in an Ashulia factory parking lot has left 7 people dead.

At least seven people were killed after a gas cylinder exploded in a lorry parked in the parking area of Pretty Group factories in Jamgora, Ashulia.

The blast triggered a massive fire that destroyed several vehicles in the open parking area used for transporting goods.

Four factories—Pretty Composite Textile Ltd, Pretty Composite Garments Ltd, Oxford Colours Ltd, and S Suhi Industrial Park Ltd—were shut down for one day following the incident.

Police confirmed that one body is at the Dhaka Medical College morgue, while six others are at the Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College morgue.

Five of the recovered bodies have not yet been identified. Most of the victims are believed to be employees of the factories' transport section.

Factory buildings remained undamaged, and production was expected to resume the following day after the temporary closure.

Savar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Saiful Islam stated that the Fire Service and Civil Defence and the Department of Labour will form probe committees to investigate the blast.

The upazila administration is assessing the damage and arranging pre-compensation for the families of the deceased.
